paragraphs.paragraph: The prophecy is delivered through Malachi and emphasizes God’s love for Israel through the distinction between Jacob and Esau. Edom’s ruin and inability to recover will show Israel God’s greatness even beyond its borders.
paragraphs.title: God’s Love for Israel and His Choice of Jacob

easy.explanation: The opening verse says, “The burden of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi.”
easy.q: Through whom was the word of the LORD delivered to Israel?
Whom did the LORD say He loved?

easy.explanation: The LORD said He had laid Esau’s mountains and heritage waste.
easy.q: What did the LORD lay waste?

medium.explanation: Israel would see the LORD magnified when it observed Edom’s desolation.
medium.q: How would Israel see that the LORD is magnified?

answers: Return and build the desolate places
medium.explanation: Edom said, “We will return and build the desolate places.”
medium.q: What did Edom say it would do after becoming impoverished?

medium.explanation: The word describes Edom as brought low and impoverished.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “impoverished” mean?

answers: Jacob was loved and Esau was hated
Jacob was distant and Esau was near
challenge.explanation: The LORD explicitly says, “I loved Jacob” and “I hated Esau.”
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between Jacob and Esau in this passage?

answers: The LORD would throw down what Edom built
Edom would become part of Israel
challenge.explanation: The LORD says, “They shall build, but I will throw down.”
challenge.q: What does the LORD’s answer to Edom show about its attempts to recover?

answers: The LORD’s greatness would be known beyond Israel’s border
challenge.explanation: Israel would recognize that the LORD is magnified even beyond its own border.
challenge.q: What does “from the border of Israel” mean in context?

paragraphs.idea: The prophecy is delivered through Malachi and emphasizes God’s love for Israel through the distinction between Jacob and Esau. Edom’s ruin and inability to recover will show Israel God’s greatness even beyond its borders.

paragraphs.paragraph: God expects honor and reverence, as a son honors his father and a servant his master, but He accuses the priests of despising His name. They dishonor the altar and place defiled bread upon it while denying their responsibility.
paragraphs.title: The Priests’ Contempt for God

answers: A son and his father, and a servant and his master
easy.explanation: The verse says, “A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master.”
easy.q: To what relationships does the LORD compare the proper response to Him?

easy.explanation: The LORD directly addresses the priests who despised His name.
easy.q: Who was accused of despising the LORD’s name?

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “Ye offer polluted bread upon mine altar.”
easy.q: What did the priests offer upon the LORD’s altar?

answers: To show that honor and fear are proper responses to Him
medium.explanation: The comparison shows that God deserves honor as a father and fear as a master.
medium.q: Why does the LORD mention a son and a servant at the beginning of His rebuke?

answers: They asked, “Wherein have we despised thy name?”
medium.explanation: The priests responded by asking how they had despised His name.
medium.q: How did the priests respond when accused of despising the LORD’s name?

medium.explanation: The word describes bread that was defiled and unfit for the altar.
medium.q: What does “polluted” mean in the phrase “polluted bread”?

answers: Disrespect toward the altar expresses disrespect toward God
challenge.explanation: Offering polluted bread upon the LORD’s altar is presented as contempt for His name.
challenge.q: What is the connection between dishonoring the altar and despising the LORD’s name?

answers: They honored the LORD but refused to work
They denied despising God’s name even though their actions dishonored Him
They admitted that the altar belonged to Edom
challenge.explanation: They asked how they had despised the LORD despite offering polluted bread and treating His table contemptuously.
challenge.q: What contradiction appears in the priests’ response?

challenge.explanation: A son honors his father, and a servant fears his master.
challenge.q: What was required of the priests according to the comparison with a son and a servant?

paragraphs.idea: God expects honor and reverence, as a son honors his father and a servant his master, but He accuses the priests of despising His name. They dishonor the altar and place defiled bread upon it while denying their responsibility.

paragraphs.paragraph: The priests offer blind, lame, and sick animals, although they would not dare give such a gift to a human governor. God rejects their offerings and would rather see the temple doors closed than witness worship without value.
paragraphs.title: Defective Offerings and Their Rejection

easy.explanation: The passage mentions the blind, the lame, and the sick.
easy.q: What kinds of animals did the priests offer for sacrifice?

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “Offer it now unto thy governor.”
easy.q: To whom did the LORD tell them to offer the defective sacrifice?

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “Neither will I accept an offering at your hand.”
easy.q: What did the LORD say about their offering?

answers: Because they would give such a gift only to a governor
Because they would not dare offer such a defective gift even to a human ruler
Because the governor was a priest
medium.explanation: The LORD asks whether their governor would be pleased with or accept such an offering.
medium.q: Why does the comparison with the governor strengthen the LORD’s criticism?

medium.explanation: They were told to beseech God that He would be gracious unto them.
medium.q: What did the priests ask God to do for them?

medium.explanation: A governor is a human ruler or official to whom they would show greater care.
medium.q: What does “governor” mean in this passage?

answers: That the temple doors be shut
That more defective animals be brought
challenge.explanation: The LORD asks who would shut the doors rather than kindle fire on His altar for nothing.
challenge.q: What does the LORD prefer to worthless altar service?

answers: The priests respected a human ruler more than the LORD
The governor was more important than the altar
The priests did not know their governor
challenge.explanation: They would not offer a defective gift to a governor, yet they offered such sacrifices to God.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between treatment of the governor and treatment of God reveal?

challenge.explanation: The LORD says He has no pleasure in them and will not accept an offering from their hand.
challenge.q: What was the result of bringing defective offerings?

paragraphs.idea: The priests offer blind, lame, and sick animals, although they would not dare give such a gift to a human governor. God rejects their offerings and would rather see the temple doors closed than witness worship without value.

paragraphs.paragraph: God’s name is great among the nations, and a pure offering is presented to Him everywhere, yet the priests in Israel treat the altar and offerings as contemptible. By bringing stolen and defective sacrifices, they show contempt for the great King whose name inspires fear among the nations.
paragraphs.title: The Greatness of God’s Name versus Its Profanation

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “My name shall be great among the Gentiles.”
easy.q: Among whom would the LORD’s name be great?

easy.explanation: The passage says that in every place incense and a pure offering would be offered.
easy.q: What would be offered to the LORD in every place?

answers: As a place no one could approach
easy.explanation: They said, “The table of the LORD is polluted,” and its fruit was contemptible.
easy.q: How did the priests regard the table of the LORD?

answers: The Gentiles offer a pure offering, while the priests bring defective sacrifices
The Gentiles close the temple, while the priests build it
The Gentiles despise God’s name, while the priests praise it
medium.explanation: The passage contrasts the greatness of God’s name among the nations with the priests’ contemptuous offerings.
medium.q: What contrast does this passage present?

answers: The torn, the lame, and the sick
medium.explanation: The priests brought that which was torn, along with the lame and the sick.
medium.q: Which offerings demonstrated the priests’ contempt?

answers: The food upon the LORD’s table
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the food or offerings associated with the LORD’s table.
medium.q: In context, what does “the fruit thereof, even his meat” refer to?

answers: The worldwide extent of the LORD’s greatness
A specific place in the temple
challenge.explanation: The phrase covers the full span from sunrise to sunset and points to the wide extent of God’s name.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “from the rising of the sun even unto the going down” emphasize?

answers: It shows contempt for the great King
It proves that the Gentiles do not worship
challenge.explanation: The LORD identifies Himself as a great King whose name is dreadful among the heathen.
challenge.q: Why is offering a stolen or defective sacrifice especially serious?

challenge.explanation: The passage says, “Cursed be the deceiver” who vows and sacrifices a corrupt thing.
challenge.q: What is the LORD’s judgment on the person who vows a proper male but sacrifices a corrupt thing?

paragraphs.idea: God’s name is great among the nations, and a pure offering is presented to Him everywhere, yet the priests in Israel treat the altar and offerings as contemptible. By bringing stolen and defective sacrifices, they show contempt for the great King whose name inspires fear among the nations.
